script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is a usage script, not a market script. Baltimore has been the run team (Henry 66 carries/301 yards, Jackson 14/127, Hill 13/57, about 61 targets in three games) and at home should try to play through Henry's early-down carries and Jackson's keepers. Tennessee has been more pass-balanced (75 targets vs 64 rushes) with Pollard the lead back (38 carries) and Tate/Robinson the target leaders, and stays involved enough in a non-blowout that Pollard keeps a normal 10-14 carry load.
script.flip1: Both Ravens centers are out (Pocic, Gwyn) and Stanley is questionable, so the interior gets disrupted: Henry's efficiency drops, Jackson scrambles more, and the game stays competitive enough that Tennessee does not abandon Pollard.
script.flip2: Baltimore scores early and leads big, closes on the ground with Henry, then rests starters. Tennessee abandons the run, Pollard's rush yards die, and the live overs become Tennessee pass volume (Tate 219 air yards, Robinson 18 targets), not the rush legs.

injury_fallout: Morning report only; inactives not locked. BAL C Ethan Pocic out (knee) and C Jovaughn Gwyn out (ankle) deplete the interior: Henry's between-the-tackles efficiency is the loser, Jackson's scramble equity and checkdowns (Andrews, Henry, Hill) are the gainers. BAL T Ronnie Stanley questionable (toe) would amplify that if he sits. BAL WR Zay Flowers questionable (hamstring) and WR Chris Moore questionable (ankle): if Flowers is limited, Andrews (18 targets) and Bateman (13) are next up, but those lines are not shown as moved. BAL LB Trey Hendrickson out (finger) removes an edge rusher, which helps Tennessee's pass protection more than any skill sleeper. TEN RB Tyjae Spears questionable (ankle): Pollard already has 38 carries to Spears' 13, so a limited Spears adds carries to Pollard rather than creating a new back. TEN S Kevin Winston Jr. questionable (shoulder) is a possible second-level loss for Baltimore's explosives if he sits. Sources: pack official injury report; TEN/BAL week 1-3 usage totals.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting in the pack, so MOFO/MOFC and man/zone are unknown. Proxy only: Baltimore blitzes 36 percent, Tennessee 21 percent.
matchup.pressure: Baltimore's 36 percent blitz has not been how to beat Cam Ward: Tennessee EPA/dropback is +0.13 vs the blitz and -0.19 with no blitz. Tennessee blitzes only 21 percent, and Baltimore is efficient either way (+0.32 vs blitz, +0.35 vs none). The Ravens' pressure problem is their own interior, not Tennessee's blitz rate.
matchup.bleeds: Baltimore run defense allows 4.16 YPC and 10 runs of 10-plus. Pass locations: middle 8.3 YPA (23 att), left 6.93 (41), right 5.34 (41); 8 passes of 20-plus. Tennessee run defense is stingier at 3.83 YPC and 7 runs of 10-plus, but leaks outside (left 7.3, right 7.37) more than the middle (6.53), with 9 passes of 20-plus.
matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is Pollard into Baltimore's run defense, not a receiver into a named corner. Tate leads Tennessee in air yards (219 on 20 targets) but Baltimore's soft pass spot is the middle, and no alignment chart maps him there. Helm (11 targets) is the structural middle/blitz fit, but his last two games were 13 and 14 yards, so that overlap is not a leg. Jackson's rush read is his own usage and the backup centers, not Tennessee bleeding quarterback runs.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the slip lost because the missing spread was a Baltimore lay of more than a touchdown. Tennessee was down two scores by halftime, Ward threw it 40 times, Pollard finished on 8 carries under 48, and Spears was active and took the passing-down snaps. Jackson's 127-yard three-game total turned out to be one long run and two quiet games, Tennessee's 3.83 YPC run defense fit the keepers, and he was done for the day in the fourth quarter with the game in hand, finishing under 31. The backup centers were adequate enough that the scramble equity never showed up.
slip_story: One competitive-game story, not a shootout and not a blowout. Pollard keeps a full early-down share against the softer run defense; Jackson's designed runs, plus any extra scrambles from Pocic and Gwyn being out, clear 31. Do not add Tennessee pass overs that need the trail-and-abandon flip, and do not add a Henry rush over that needs a healthy interior. No bets placed; both legs are candidates for the human, with Jackson flagged.
